key_insight: JEV matched Qwen Flash on two trial-prescreening datasets and outperformed it on MIMIC-III, with lower observed latency and estimated cost.
clinical_relevance: JEV could support criterion-level trial prescreening by flagging potential information gaps for human review, but this study did not evaluate cancer drug discovery or clinical outcomes.
method: Retrospectively compared non-generative JEV with schema-constrained Qwen Flash against reference labels.
Assessed criteria individually and in batches sharing patient context.
Evaluated under strict Zero Data Retention policies.
evidence_signal: Across 2,048 patient-condition pairs from TrialGPT and MIMIC-derived datasets, JEV achieved batch macro-F1 of 0.768 versus Qwen's 0.534 on MIMIC-III, with similar scores on the other datasets and 53%–74% lower estimated cost per condition.
watch_item: Errors in interpreting clinical evidence require verification against patient records before outputs inform eligibility decisions.
paper_title: Can JEV Support Clinical Trial Criteria Assessment?
